chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: similar to it.
Except that he عليه السلام said: ‘Like this, and like this, and like this, and like this’—meaning from before him, and behind him, and from his right, and from his left.

key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: similar to it; indicating a parallel narration in wording or meaning
key_terms.مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ: from in front of him; the direction before a person
key_terms.هَكَذَا: like this; an indicated gesture or demonstrative expression

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase ‘like this and like this’ mean in the hadith of Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report preserves a variant wording in which Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام gestures in four directions to indicate comprehensiveness. In the chapter context, it emphasizes surrounding and complete regard for the rights connected to the Imam and the people.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> similar to it,
except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Like this, and like this, and the like this and like this’, meaning from in front of him, and behind him, and from his right and from his left’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Hamza from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) a similar hadith

except that he has said, “this way, this way, this way and this way, meaning thereby front, back, right and left.” Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar from certain members of our people from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas‘ada ibn sadaqa from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) has said, ‘Do not be deceitful to your leaders, do not confuse your guides, do not be ignorant of your Imams and do not cut off the rope of your unity, least you will fail and be disgraced. On such foundation your affairs must be based and you must strictly live within such system. Had you been able to observe what those who lived before had observed and who had disregarded what you want to be accepted you would have acted fast, came out and listened. However, you can not observe what they had observed but the curtain will soon be removed.’”
